articles.content: Prior was -135.9B That's going leave a dent in GDP forecasts. Elsewhere: Wholesale inventories +0.9% vs +0.8% prior Retail inventories ex autos +0.6% vs +0.7% prior The inventory data should somewhat offset the drag from trade. For background, the advance international trade in goods report is published by the Census Bureau at 8:30 am ET as part of its Advance Economic Indicators release, roughly four weeks after the reference month ends. It's the earliest monthly read on US trade flows and lands alongside advance estimates for wholesale and retail inventories, making it a key input for GDP tracking. The headline is the seasonally adjusted US goods trade deficit, the gap between the value of goods imported and exported. Both sides are broken down into six end-use categories: foods, feeds and beverages; industrial supplies and materials; capital goods; automotive vehicles, parts and engines; consumer goods; and other goods. The figures are in nominal dollars on a Census basis. The advance report covers goods only. Services, where the US runs a surplus in areas such as travel, financial services and intellectual property, are added in the full international trade report from the Census Bureau and the Bureau of Economic Analysis about a week later. That report also revises the advance goods numbers and adds country-level detail. For markets, the main relevance is GDP. Net exports are a component of growth, so a wider goods deficit generally subtracts from GDP and a narrower one adds to it. Paired with the inventory data released at the same time, the report frequently leads economists and nowcasting models such as the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow to revise their quarterly estimates. Trade data have been unusually volatile. Surges in imports ahead of tariffs, followed by sharp pullbacks, have caused large swings in the deficit and in quarterly GDP. Big movements in nonmonetary gold, recorded under industrial supplies, have added noise, and economists often exclude gold to judge the underlying trend This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

articles.desc: Friendship rides alongside politics in Agartala, rival candidates tour booths on two-wheeler
articles.content: Friendship rides alongside politics in Agartala, rival candidates tour booths on two-wheeler | Guwahati News - The Times of India Friendship rides alongside politics in Agartala, rival candidates tour booths on two-wheeler Friendship rides alongside politics in Agartala, rival candidates tour booths on two-wheeler Agartala: While much of Tripura’s civic poll campaign was overshadowed by allegations of violence and attacks on opposition candidates, polling agents and voters, Ward No-16 of Agartala offered a different picture on Friday. candidate Pinaki Chakraborty was seen giving his rival, Bijoy Biswas, a ride on his two-wheeler between polling stations in the Ramnagar area. Pinaki is the youngest candidate in the Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC) election and was fielded by BJP in place of outgoing mayor Dipak Majumdar. Dressed in white shirts, the two travelled around Ramnagar, visiting polling stations and checking on the voting process. The sight drew attention at a time when reports of tension and confrontations were emerging from other parts of the city. Chakraborty told TOI that their friendship began during their school days at Umakanta Academy and continued through their time at MBB College. Different political affiliations, he said, had never weakened their bond, including during the election campaign. Describing polling day as a festival of democracy, Chakraborty said they wanted to spend part of the day together in a spirit of friendship and brotherhood. He also spoke about building a “Green Ramnagar”, where people from different political backgrounds could work together for the welfare of the neighbourhood. Biswas said ideological differences should not damage personal relationships or disturb peace in the community. From the beginning of the campaign, he said, he had appealed to all candidates to keep politics healthy and peaceful. Political rivals could still discuss issues affecting residents, he said. The two have remained in regular contact and, according to Biswas, could continue working together for Ramnagar regardless of who wins the ward. He said politics should focus on serving people rather than creating conflict. Neither candidate predicted the outcome, saying the verdict rested with the voters and would be known once votes were counted on Dec 2. Their interaction stood in contrast to the bitter exchanges often seen during election campaigns. While representing different parties, both candidates presented a message of political rivalry without personal animosity. Stay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Michael Nielsen says he took down his neural networks book over AI risks
articles.desc: Nielsen says he no longer wants his book to help train people for frontier AI work.
articles.content: Michael Nielsen says he pulled his neural-net book rather than help the AI race · Digg Michael Nielsen says he has taken down Neural Networks and Deep Learning because he doesn't want to help train people for frontier AI work. His withdrawal notice argues that development is outpacing society's defenses, while acknowledging AI's benefits and the costs of slowing it down. He tells anyone considering frontier-lab work: don't go. because he no longer wants to help educate people who contribute to frontier AI development. He announced the withdrawal in a November 27 post, linking to the book's website. In the website notice, dated November 2026, he writes: “I don't wish to help (even in a very small way) train people to contribute to this work, and so I've taken the book down.” He's talking about educating people, not preventing AI models from training on the text. Nielsen says he wrote the book between 2011 and 2015, when he expected artificial general intelligence based on neural networks to remain decades away. He anticipated remarkable benefits and significant challenges, but thought society would likely address those challenges as capabilities developed. “My views have changed,” he writes. Nielsen argues that development has moved much faster than he expected, leaving humanity too little time to prepare. His central concern isn't simply that people might lose control of an advanced AI system. It's that artificial superintelligence could enable destructive technologies faster than institutions can develop defenses, whether humans or uncontrolled machines wield them. Making individual AI systems behave as intended is important, Nielsen argues, but won't resolve the broader danger. In his view, this technical alignment work makes systems more acceptable to consumers and governments, speeding development while society's defenses lag. He also challenges the argument that safety-minded people should build frontier AI because someone less responsible would otherwise do it. Nielsen asks what evidence would demonstrate that their participation actually reduces risk compared with the alternatives. Good intentions, in his account, aren't enough. Nielsen describes AI's overall impact to date as net positive and acknowledges that a significant slowdown would be costly. He still considers frontier AI development too reckless to support. The withdrawal doubles as an anti-recruitment message—not exactly a glowing careers-page testimonial. “So, don't go to work for a frontier lab,” he writes, urging people working on AI to focus on slowing it down and opposing the labs instead. He closes: “I very much hope I'm wrong about all of this. But this is how I see the situation.” I took down my old book on neural nets: https://neuralnetworksanddeeplearning.com @michael_nielsen Neural Networks and Deep Learning (2011–2015) was free online for a decade. He took it down this November so it wouldn't, even slightly, help train people for frontier lab work. Copies will keep circulating. The dated withdrawal notice is what's new. articles.title: Voices: I let Meta’s new AI agent Muse organise my life. It started building files on my children
articles.desc: I called my agent Mouse. I gave her a superhero cape. She was cute and very, very efficient. But maybe I went too far, writes Jacqui Merrington
articles.content: I let Meta’s new AI agent Muse organise my life: It started building files on my children | The Independent Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. have a new companion named Mouse. She’s smart, bossy and a little bit too inquisitive. In fact, in three days I think she’s found out more about me than my own husband. , the agent is designed to help people live their lives, streamlining everything from everyday scheduling to shopping. It’s had 10 million downloads in the US since it was introduced in September, making it one of the fastest-growing apps of all time. ICO (Information Commissioners Office) has expressed concern about its rollout in the UK , worried that it could lead to users handing over personal and intimate data or giving the tool the power to do things they don’t actually want. I’ve always been somewhat cavalier with my personal effects. I’ll happily open my home up to complete strangers, share an embarrassing picture on or even put my bank statements straight into the recycling without shredding them. I figure there’s little anyone could gain from stealing my identity – with any luck they might even decide to top up my bank balance while they’re rummaging through my financial affairs. So I decide to go all in on Muse to see what will happen if I hand over the keys to my digital life. And where better to start than by giving her full access to the most terrifying place I know: my personal email inbox. Setting up Muse is ridiculously easy - I download the app, and she (he? it?) asks me for a name. I’d like a small friendly animal with a bit of sass, so I create Mouse. ? Or hand me something else on your list?” I have to admit, even I have a slight hesitation about opening up my Gmail. Initially I opt to put the Mouse in read-only mode. She begins sweeping through my overflowing personal inbox. Within moments, Mouse presents me with a psychological profile based purely on my newsletter subscriptions: She promptly schedules a daily Gmail summary for 8:12 am every morning around the issues that she feels are most important to me – news, journalism and climate. At one point, I accidentally enable voice mode, and Mouse overhears me talking about football. Suddenly, she decides I need daily football scores. I don’t, but if Mouse insists, fine. So she adds them to my daily summary. Next comes the reckoning: Mouse discovers 4,189 messages in my inbox from the last 30 days alone, estimating I was subscribed to between 550 and 600 newsletters and promotions. She prompts me to switch from read-only mode to full archive and send privileges. I barely hesitate this time. What’s the point of an assistant that can’t actually do stuff? With a twitch of her over-animated whiskers, she quickly begins to suggest emails I should unsubscribe from and scuttles off to get it sorted. Deciding to push her further, I instruct her to search for promotional emails received prior to 2026. She uncovers more than 25,000 (cue face with peeking eye emoji). I figure that’s a little ambitious even for an AI agent to complete in one go, so I ask her to break the task into chunks. She promptly trashes 19,143 promotional emails. It’s impressive, but not yet a true game-changer. So I ask Mouse directly what it would take for her to become indispensable to me. “Good question — and honestly, the inbox work today is a good test case for it. Indispensable, for me, wouldn't be doing more random tasks. It would be learning what you actually read and care about, and quietly filtering out the rest so nothing important slips past you.” She then maps out a roadmap of how she plans to run my life: Keeping your inbox clear, and the daily 8:12 summary so new newsletters and promotions don't pile

Below it, wide multi-lane highways and elevated curved interchange loops carry traffic over greenery, wetlands, and the river corridor under a clear blue. (TOI Photo: Delhi News) Punishing working hours, intense pressure to meet financial targets, unhygienic conditions, limited food, and strict curbs on mobile phones and family contact — this is how 164 foreign nationals were allegedly kept in illegal confinement to run a cyber fraud operation out of a building in Noida’s Sector 136. smashed the racket on Thursday in an operation carried out by a team supervised by special CP (crime) HGS Dhaliwal, rescuing 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians, including 21 women. According to police sources, the recruits were allegedly trained in Malaysia and Cambodia before being brought to India. Many had limited educational qualifications, ranging from Class IX to Class XII, and were reportedly unaware of the nature of the work they had been hired for. Cops suspect the recruits were chosen because their familiarity with the language and culture of their home countries made it easier to win the trust of potential victims. The case points to a possible reversal in the modus operandi of international cyber fraud networks. Earlier, Indians were lured to foreign countries to target fellow citizens back home. In this case, Malaysians and Indonesians were allegedly brought to India to cheat people in their respective countries. Investigators of the interstate cell of Delhi Police’s crime branch found that the recruits were given scripts to approach targets on social media and gradually build trust before pitching fake investment opportunities. They were allegedly instructed to pose as women and start chats with casual messages like “Hi” or “Hello”. If questioned, they would claim the message was sent by mistake, using it as an excuse to keep talking until the target was persuaded to invest, sources said. The probe also revealed that fraudulent websites and APK-based applications were used to dupe people. Working conditions at the Noida premises have emerged as a major focus of the probe. Several rescued individuals alleged they were forced to work from 7.30 am to 10.30 pm daily under a memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed during recruitment that laid down strict rules. Many claimed they faced verbal abuse, harassment, and even physical assault if they failed to perform. “They worked in unhygienic conditions, with food packets and drinks scattered across computers and tables,” sources said, adding that recruits were given limited portions during their three daily meals and forced to work an extra hour if they missed targets. Their mobile phone access was restricted, and they were barred from speaking to colleagues inside the building or contacting their families. “One of them claimed he was brought to India on the pretext of participating in a gaming competition, after which his passport was taken away,” sources said. “They also claimed they were made to smoke or consume substances to keep them awake,” a source added. Investigators suspect unemployed youngsters were spotted through social media posts and reels indicating they were looking for jobs, before recruiters approached them with offers. Police are also probing claims that some recruits had previously been deported. Financial details uncovered during the probe show the scale of the syndicate. articles.title: Top Treasury Official Is Too Busy Vibe Coding a Crappy Video Game Clone Instead of Addressing a Historic Hack
articles.desc: Maybe he's "vibe working." The post Top Treasury Official Is Too Busy Vibe Coding a Crappy Video Game Clone Instead of Addressing a Historic Hack appeared first on Futurism.
articles.content: Top Treasury Official Is Too Busy Vibe Coding a Crappy Video Game Clone Instead of Addressing a Historic Hack We’re all guilty of procrastinating. But not all of us are in charge of running the treasury of the wealthiest nation in the world. As the Treasury Department scrambled to address a major hack on its internal services, its chief information officer, Sam Corcos, was preoccupied with a little sidequest: vibe coding his own video game, Corcos, a cofounder of a health tech startup called Levels, was first brought on as a DOGE hire near the start of Trump’s second term and has been spearheading the deployment of AI across the government ever since. He apparently loves using AI in his free time, too. On GitHub, Corcos has been using Anthropic’s Claude AI to push regular updates to a project he calls “Legatum,” a clone of the iconic “Civilization” strategy games. And we do mean regular. On Tuesday the Treasury Department’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), which handles sensitive information and reports about serious financial crimes, disclosed that it was dealing with a “cybersecurity incident” that led to “unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.” And in the midst of this — not to mention that have beset the tech sector and government agencies over the past few weeks — Corcos was still fiddling with AI to build his game. Update logs on GitHub show that during and after the hack, while the agency was still dealing with the fallout, Corcos released balance patches for the game, new theme music for the Aztecs — AI-generated, of course — and overhauled its in-game tooltips system, per He also enthusiastically released a new special unit for Egypt, right at the same time that the Treasury Department warned that FinCEN was taking some of its systems offline “as a proactive measure.” As word spread online of Corcos’s extracurricular, or perhaps on the clock, activity, trolls and angry netizens began piling into the GitHub’s project’s discussion board for flagging issues with the game. “The Treasury Department is being hacked and you are vibe coding a video game instead,” . “Proposed Solution: Delete this repo and fix the security issues at the Treasury Department.” Corcos, apparently still having plenty of time on his hands, hasn’t helped his case by individually replying to and hiding the troll’s posts — a task that he’s automated with even more AI. “Closing as off-topic,” he responded to the above post this morning. “This tracker is for bugs and ideas about the Legatum game,” he added, with a signature reading “Generated by Claude Code.” The jokes continue to write themselves even more readily than his vibe coded video game. His last tweet, spotted, was a defense of DOGE once again demanding federal workers to send in written letters explaining what they do. “I believe it is reasonable to ask employees what they are working on,” Corcos It Turns Out Binance’s $6 Billion Hack Happened Because Its Employees Were Vibe Coding

Why Temperature-Controlled Logistics Is Essential Biopharmaceutical products often require specific temperature conditions to maintain their quality and stability. Vaccines, biologics, certain medicines, and other sensitive healthcare products can experience degradation when exposed to unsuitable environmental conditions. Cold chain logistics involves specialized storage, packaging, transportation, and monitoring systems designed to maintain appropriate temperature ranges throughout the supply chain. The process begins at manufacturing facilities and continues through distribution centers, transportation networks, warehouses, and healthcare providers. Maintaining temperature consistency is important because exposure to unsuitable conditions can affect product quality and create challenges for pharmaceutical manufacturers.
